headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, and the crowd is greedy for good reason: the tape mostly agrees with it
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it's lopsided in a way that matters. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages; only DOGE and ADA sit below. ETH, SOL, and BNB carry golden crosses on top of that. This is a market where the trend-followers have the wind at their back almost everywhere except two of the seven names on this board. Bitcoin itself is down -0.2% on the day but up 3.3% on the week and up 24.6% on the month, so the daily wobble is noise sitting on top of a trend that hasn't changed character.

Momentum is where the first real tension shows up. BTC's RSI-14 at 72.1 is deep into overbought territory, and its MACD is above signal, so trend and momentum are pulling the same direction there, no argument. But look at ETH, SOL, and BNB: RSI readings of 68.3, 67.5, and 69.5 are hot, yet all three have MACD below signal. That's a quiet divergence worth naming: price and the moving averages say uptrend, but the momentum oscillator on the shorter-term MACD is cooling even as RSI stays warm. It doesn't say what happens next, it says the rally's engine is idling a bit while the odometer keeps turning.

Positioning adds another wrinkle. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0032% per 8 hours (3.5% annualized), cheap by crypto standards, and the long/short account ratio is actually below parity at 0.92, meaning more short accounts than long ones even as price grinds higher. Liquidations in the last hour skew hard toward shorts getting run over ($793K liquidated versus $21K of longs), which fits a market that keeps punishing the skeptics. ETH funding runs hotter at 6.9% annualized with a long/short ratio of 1.17, so leverage there is more one-sided. XRP and DOGE funding both sit at 11% annualized with long/short ratios above 2, crowded and expensive by comparison, the kind of positioning that's fuel for a squeeze in either direction rather than something stable.

The flow picture backs the tape rather than fights it. BTC spot ETFs posted a net inflow of $730.8M on Sep 3, and the five-session net is $610.2M, same direction, so that's a real trend, not a one-day print. ETH ETFs took in $141.4M on the same day with a five-session net of $291.5M. On the whale side, the last 48 hours show $27.0M net moving off exchanges in BTC, and the most recent weekly window (week ending Sep 04) shows $223M net moving off exchanges too, a reversal from the three prior weeks (Aug 14, Aug 21, Aug 28) which all saw hundreds of millions to over a billion dollars moving onto exchanges. Coins are just starting to head back to cold storage after weeks of the opposite. Stablecoin float is up 1.44% over 30 days to $310.2B, dry powder that's growing, not shrinking.

Sentiment sits at 74, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 74. Normally that's the moment to ask whether the crowd is ahead of the money. Here it mostly isn't: ETF flows are net positive and multi-day, whale flows just flipped toward exchanges leaving rather than arriving, and six of seven majors hold their 200-day trend. The greed reading and the tape are, for once, telling a similar story rather than arguing with each other.

What to watch: whether ETH, SOL, and BNB's MACD-below-signal condition resolves by MACD crossing back up (momentum catching up to trend) or by RSI cooling toward it (trend catching up to momentum). Also watch BTC's long/short ratio, currently below 1 even as price holds its 200-day line: a flip toward more longs than shorts alongside rising funding would mark a shift from cheap, skeptical positioning to something more crowded. And watch whether the week-ending-Sep-04 shift toward off-exchange BTC flow extends into another weekly print or reverts to the onto-exchanges pattern seen in the three weeks before it.
